sections.html:
Middletown stands on the Connecticut River's west bank in Middlesex County, some 16 miles below Hartford. The 2020 census found 47,717 people spread across 42.36 square miles. Of 21,671 housing units counted that year, 54% were owner-occupied. Route 9 runs beside the river and splits the city, and Interstate 91 clips only the western edge.

The river has shaped the housing stock. Floods came in 1927 and 1936, the 1938 hurricane followed, and a 1950s highway later walled the city off from its waterfront. Older riverside streets carry that history, and a seller near the water will hear questions about flooding and drainage.

sections.h2: Mill rates and how the tax is figured
sections.html:
Property is assessed at 70% of its value, and the assessment is multiplied by the mill rate to produce the tax. On the October 1, 2025 grand list, for bills effective July 1, 2026, the combined real estate rate varies with the fire district around the house. The city's mill rates page has the current numbers.

Fire districtCity mill rateDistrict rateCombined real estate rate
City Fire District33.307.5040.800
South Fire District33.305.31138.611
Westfield Fire District33.302.08435.384

Registered vehicles are capped at 32.46. In the City Fire District the fire tax rides on the city bill. The South Fire and Westfield Fire Districts bill and collect for themselves, which means owners there get two bills.

sections.h2: Due dates, interest and who gets the bill
sections.html:
The fiscal year is July 1 to June 30, and half the tax is due on each of July 1 and January 1. If an installment is still unpaid on the first business day of the next month, interest of 1.5% per month (18% a year) is charged from the original due date. The Tax Collector's tax information page explains the rest.

  • A bill that never arrived does not cancel the tax or the interest, and the office provides copies free.
  • Banks and mortgage companies that escrow must request bills each year from the Tax Collector.
  • The bill is addressed to whoever owned the property on the October 1 grand list date, and state law keeps that name on it until the next assessment date.
  • If you pay off a mortgage, tell the office so it can update its records.

A sale in between can leave the previous owner's name on the bill, so ask the collector who actually receives it.

sections.h2: Selling a Middletown house with tax owed
sections.html:
Start with a payoff request to the Tax Collector. At closing the title company takes that amount from your proceeds, so you do not have to find the money beforehand. Work in this order.

  1. Identify your fire district, since it decides how many bills you have.
  2. In the South Fire or Westfield Fire District, request that district's balance separately.
  3. See whether a mortgage servicer still gets the bill, and report a paid-off loan to the office.
  4. Hand every number to your closing attorney in writing.

Plan the timing around the two installment dates as well. A closing shortly before July 1 or January 1 leaves a fresh installment about to come due, and the buyer and seller should agree in writing who covers it. A closing just after a due date, with interest running from the first of the next month, calls for a payoff that is accurate to the day.

Bring the deed, a photo ID and, for an estate, the papers that name who can sign. The Middletown town clerk records the deed.

Every Middletown house sits in one of three fire districts. The city's 33.30 is the same in each, and only the fire piece changes: 7.50 in the City Fire District, 5.311 in the South Fire District and 2.084 in the Westfield Fire District. Two houses with equal assessments can therefore carry different tax bills, and a buyer comparing listings will see it. Learn your district before you advertise.

Unsure which applies? The Assessor or Tax Collector can read it off the parcel. Owners in the South Fire and Westfield Fire Districts should also keep the district bill apart from the city bill, because paying one does not clear the other.

sections.h2: Mortgages, escrow and the record owner
sections.html:
Many Middletown bills are sent to a bank, not the owner. Banks and mortgage companies that escrow must ask the Tax Collector for each year's bills, so when a mortgage is paid off, call the office and stop the bill going to a servicer that is no longer involved. A house sold mid-year can also produce a bill under the previous owner's name. That is normal but confusing, so decide at closing who pays the next installment and record the answer in the closing paperwork.

If a bill never shows up, do not wait it out. The tax and interest are still owed. Request a free copy, confirm the account number, and pay before the first business day of the following month.

A sale goes faster with a short folder. Put in the latest bills for the city and, if it applies, the fire district, the deed, a government ID, and any letter from a lender about escrow. For an estate, add the papers naming the representative. Having these ready lets the Tax Collector answer a payoff request in one call and lets your attorney see every open item at once. It also shows a buyer that the house has no hidden balance, which keeps the deal moving when other parts of the sale hit a snag.

Form OP-236, the state's conveyance tax return, goes in at the time the deed is recorded. Middletown's number on the Department of Revenue Services list is 083. The state page names two exemptions worth knowing: a principal residence deeded in lieu of foreclosure, and one sold for less than the mortgages and priority tax liens add up to.

Selling an inherited house? Middletown shares a probate court district with Cromwell, Portland, Middlefield and Haddam. Nobody can sign the deed until the estate has an authorized representative, so begin that step before you look for a buyer, and ask the Tax Collector to mail bills to that person while the estate stays open.

Typical Middletown sellers are owners behind on tax, heirs holding a house they would rather not keep, and owners who live elsewhere. Cash Home Buyers buys Middletown houses as-is in each of those cases. You skip repairs and showings, and the title company settles what is owed from the proceeds. Whether that beats listing depends on the repair bill, the showings you are willing to host and how long you can carry the house through further installments.

faqs.q: When are Middletown real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: July 1 and January 1. Interest at 1.5% per month starts if an installment is still unpaid on the first business day of the next month.
Property is assessed at 70% of its value, and that assessment is multiplied by the mill rate.

faqs.q: What is the Middletown mill rate?
faqs.a: On the October 1, 2025 grand list the combined real estate rate is 40.800 mills in the City Fire District, 38.611 in the South Fire District and 35.384 in the Westfield Fire District.

faqs.q: Do some Middletown owners get two tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Those two districts bill and collect on their own, apart from the city bill.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Middletown house if I owe tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing normally settles the tax out of what you receive, with the title company making the payment.
